patch: Killswitch bypass-route assertion could never match a 0.0.0.0/0 management allow-CIDR: we install 0.0.0.0/0 but iproute2 renders it back as `default`, and route_destination_matches_rendered compared the two literally (phase10.rs). It handled the /32 host-route quirk but not the default-route one. Every reconcile therefore failed its killswitch assertion and restricted the daemon, so `route advertise 0.0.0.0/0` was refused with "daemon is in restricted-safe mode". Fix: match `default` for prefix /0 on 0.0.0.0 and ::. Proven on a guest: `ip route replace 0.0.0.0/0 dev enp0s1 table 51820` reads back as `default dev enp0s1 scope link`. NOTE: the privileged-helper "truncated frame header" deaths seen alongside this are a SEPARATE fault, still open.

Patch: widen the detector and route 7 exposed sites through REMOTE_RUSTYNET_BIN (8973546).

patch: nc-free fallback (ae678de) IS reached (error changed from 'nc not installed' to 'exit None') — so the nc gap is fixed, but the /dev/tcp construct wrapped bash in `timeout`, and bash waits on its child cat; a blocked socket read ignores SIGTERM to the parent so timeout escalated to SIGKILL and lost the reply (exit None/signal). FIX (next commit): move timeout onto the READ cat itself (`cat >&3; timeout {t} cat <&3`) so SIGTERM interrupts the blocked read (EINTR) and cat exits with the bytes read, mirroring nc -w. Verified live on rocky: bash /dev/tcp supported + the corrected construct returns a server response cleanly. Re-running to confirm anchor green.

patch: ROOT CAUSE captured (journal poller). During the network_flap WG-block (nft drop udp dport 51820), the client daemon's traversal/reconcile keeps calling initiate_peer_handshake -> userspace-shared UDP send_to -> EPERM 'Operation not permitted (os error 1)' (nft drop). Each is counted a reconcile failure (restrict_recoverable + promote_to_permanent_if_over_limit); after 5 the daemon is promoted to restrict_permanent (FailClosed, NEVER recovers), so after network_flap unblocks WG the tunnel never recovers -> test fails. REAL availability bug: a transient network blip permanently bricks the daemon. FIX DIRECTION (§9 security-sensitive): a TRANSIENT connectivity/send failure (EPERM/unreachable) during reconcile must be recoverable and NOT escalate to permanent lockout — distinct from a trust/membership VERIFICATION failure (missing/bad-signature) which correctly can. Do not weaken verification fail-closed; only stop connectivity failures from counting toward permanent promotion (or recover from permanent on next successful reconcile). Investigating the exact reconcile classification before patching.

patch: Lab-side ownership repair to test a diagnosis, NOT a code fix: chown root:rustynetd /etc/rustynet on debian-headless-2 and debian-headless-4. Both nodes had uid=987(rustynetd) gid=0(root), i.e. owner and group swapped from the documented intent. ops_install_systemd.rs:131-136 provisions /etc/rustynet as uid 0 / gid rustynetd / 0750, and secret_material.rs:34-35 overrides the custody policy to required_directory_mode=0o750 specifically for that directory. Commit 306575df (2026-07-30, after the 8a2d6136 baseline) added the uid half of the custody check (rustynet-crypto/src/lib.rs:1770-1779: directory_uid and file_uid must both equal the EFFECTIVE uid). The stage runs 'ops e2e-issue-traversal-bundles-from-env' as root via run_root, so with the directory owned by 987 the root-owned /etc/rustynet/assignment.signing.secret became undecryptable and the stage failed after 20 retries. Re-running to confirm the ownership is the whole cause. The custody check itself is correct hardening and must not be weakened.

patch: FIXED (environment): rocky-utm-1's clock was 8455s (2h21m) behind the host, so a correctly-issued auto-tunnel bundle read as future dated and the daemon failed closed with 'auto-tunnel bundle is future dated'. That is correct fail-closed behaviour -- a future-dated bundle is a tamper signal -- but the operator saw only 'daemon socket failed to become available after 40 attempts' 151 minutes later, with the real cause invisible. Diagnosis: all four of rocky's chrony sources agreed on -8455s while NONE was selected (no ^* marker), so timedatectl reported 'System clock synchronized: yes' and the correction was never applied; hwclock agreed with the wrong time, so the RTC was genuinely off. Remediated by stepping the clock and syncing the RTC; the whole five-guest fleet now reads skew 0s. The code gap is that nothing checks clock skew in preflight, so this surfaces as an unrelated socket timeout after a long retry loop.

patch: QH-45 fix was INCOMPLETE in this run; corrected since. That commit added counter to two emitters and only the forward one had been allowlisted, so this run cleared apply_firewall_killswitch and died one step later in apply_nat_forwarding with the error string changing from firewall apply failed to nat apply failed and nothing else. Adversarial review caught it; a fix that only moves an error string is not a fix. Both arms are now allowlisted -- forward iifname X oifname X counter accept, and postrouting iifname X oifname X counter masquerade -- each requiring the two interface names to be equal, matching the emitters which pass one interface into both slots. Authority is unchanged: guards are byte-identical to the pre-existing non-counter siblings, the slice patterns are fixed-arity so counter name and counter packets forms cannot reach them, and is_interface_name is charset-bounded so an nft wildcard is unreachable (now pinned by a test).

patch: none: QH-46, diagnosis advanced and two earlier hypotheses refuted by measurement. The client reaches the entry's mesh address (reply TTL 64) and never the final exit's (no reply, 11 attempts over 96s), so client-to-entry works and entry-to-exit does not. Live sampling during the stage shows the entry IS forwarding -- hairpin rule at 27 packets, 2052 bytes, ip_forward=1 -- so per_hop_ttl_decrement=-1 is arithmetic on an unanswered probe, not evidence of no forwarding. Next: capture the client's WireGuard peer set and AllowedIPs live to determine whether the exit's mesh IP is routed via the entry at all.

patch: none: QH-46 diagnosis corrected. The exit's missing client peer is BY DESIGN -- the two-hop test documents that the entry masquerades the hairpin and that SNAT is what gives the exit a route back, which is why the exit's peers deliberately carry only entry/32 and second_client/32. With both QH-45 allowlist arms landed the NAT apply is clean, yet the proof still fails, so the masquerade installs and traffic still does not complete. Next capture is on the ENTRY: serving_exit_node plus the postrouting counter, since both hairpin rules are gated by allow_tunnel_relay_forward. Counter at zero means the SNAT is installed but not matching; rule absent means the entry is not being told it serves an exit.

patch: environment gap, not code — root cause isolated and remedied downstream. The identical failure recurred as livelab-1787884299-4b0d18aa668d::bootstrap_hosts, where it was isolated: a stale /etc/default/rustynetd left by an earlier cross-network run pinned RUSTYNET_EGRESS_INTERFACE=rustynet-vx0, and install-systemd resolve_egress_interface prefers existing_env over live detection, so it demanded a vxlan link that no longer existed (ensure_interface_exists, crates/rustynet-cli/src/ops_install_systemd.rs:2051; VXLAN_LINK_NAME, crates/rustynet-cli/src/vm_lab/orchestrator/stage/cross_network/substrate.rs:34). No code change was required for the bootstrap failure itself; the cleanup_hosts gap that leaves the residue behind is already tracked as a follow-up on that stub. patch: none (triage-only run, no code changed): the red is HONEST and is the first live macOS exercise of the QH-39 scutil-based resolver observation. macos-utm-1/DnsFailclosed failed with drift_reason "macOS loopback resolver is not advertised by /usr/sbin/scutil --dns". Reproduced by hand on the guest: /etc/resolv.conf carries the rustynet protected-mode marker with "nameserver 127.0.0.1", while /usr/sbin/scutil --dns resolver #1 reports nameserver[0]=1.1.1.1, nameserver[1]=8.8.8.8. On macOS /etc/resolv.conf is a configd-generated compatibility shim and is NOT the system resolver, so writing it does not redirect resolution; the pre-QH-39 collector hardcoded loopback_resolver_advertised=true whenever the file merely read (macos_dns_failclosed.rs:117-138 before the fix) and therefore returned a false green here. The new derivation from the independent scutil source (macos_dns_failclosed.rs:183-207, read at :230-246) correctly reds and the command exits policy_reject (78). So: the checker is behaving as designed and the underlying macOS DNS fail-closed enforcement gap it now reveals is the real defect. Not environmental, not role-election plumbing. Classified macOS-specific product gap; written up with file:line in documents/operations/active/MacCellsHarvest_2026-08-28.md.

patch: REAL product defect (not environmental; NOT closed by Gap A's enforce refresh, which landed and whose 'signed state refresh completed reason=command' fired successfully this run). Guest sampler evidence over the run window: the macOS client's networksetup loopback pin WAS applied (eth-dns=127.0.0.1 in 33 samples) and the daemon ran under launchd (pid in 38 samples), but the pf com.rustynet DNS-block anchor was NEVER populated (pf-rules=0 in all 656 samples) and the scutil PRIMARY resolver was NEVER loopback (0 samples). Hypothesis: for a plain mesh CLIENT (ExitMode::Off) killswitch_spec generates no DNS-block rules and the loopback DNS proxy is not the primary resolver, so apply_dns_protection pins to a non-primary/absent loopback resolver. Fix is DIAGNOSE-FIRST product work (design -> review -> code per the operating contract); do NOT weaken the verifier. See MacosClientDnsFailclosedDiagnosis_2026-09-02.md (in progress).

error: macos-utm-1/MeshStatus: validation not passed; macos-utm-1/DnsFailclosed: validation not passed
patch: The merged DNS three-state fix (345fe219) is behaving CORRECTLY and more securely, and its live proof exposed a DEEPER pre-existing defect. Daemon log on macos-utm-1: 'dns apply failed: the loopback DNS resolver on 127.0.0.1:53535 did not answer' -> apply rolls back fail-closed -> restrict_recoverable -> node PERMANENTLY restricted, so BOTH macos-utm-1/DnsFailclosed AND macos-utm-1/MeshStatus fail (a restricted node cannot mesh). The fix's verify_loopback_resolver_live probe (phase10.rs ~:4520, called first by apply_scoped_resolver_only) sends an A query for the mesh zone root to :53535 and requires an answer; over ~30s it never answered. ROOT: the macOS mesh CLIENT's loopback DNS resolver at 127.0.0.1:53535 does not SERVE (the daemon binds the socket at daemon.rs:12209 but nothing answers). The OLD code masked this (pinned general DNS to a dead :53, never probed :53535 = fail-OPEN); reverting would restore that leak, so do NOT revert. TWO open questions for the fix: (1) WHY does the client resolver not serve (serving loop not started for a client? no DNS zone loaded at bootstrap? apply-ordering runs the probe before the resolver serves?); (2) should a client DNS-apply failure restrict the WHOLE node/mesh, or fail only the DNS posture while keeping mesh connectivity? patch: Fixed a bootstrap readiness race: the Windows daemon-readiness probe gated bootstrap on wireguard.pub being present but not non-empty, and the daemon writes the key asynchronously at startup, so bootstrap passed while wireguard.pub was still empty and collect_pubkeys (which does not retry, unlike Linux) read an empty key and failed base64 decode with empty base64 input. Commit e1bdaeb8 makes the readiness probe also require wireguard.pub non-empty via Get-Content plus IsNullOrWhiteSpace, so bootstrap-ready means the pubkey is actually available. Verified on the guest that wireguard.pub is a valid 45-char key. fmt, the strengthened readiness-probe pinning test, and clippy all pass. Reached only because the apparmor build fix and key-custody fix let Windows bootstrap pass for the first time.

error: windows-x86-1: protocol error: node still dirty after cleanup: 1 leftover RustyNet firewall rule(s); default outbound policy left blocking; RustyNet service still running
patch: Fixed a Windows cleanup race that left the node dirty (service running + default-outbound blocking) and failed both end-of-run cleanup and the next run cleanup_hosts, bricking the guest. cleanup_runtime_state stopped the RustyNet daemon and relay best-effort then immediately ran the dataplane reset; Stop-Service only initiates the stop, so the reset could clear the killswitch while the daemon was still up and the daemon reconcile loop re-applied the default-deny outbound policy right after. Commit bfa4b80a adds a bounded wait (windows_wait_services_stopped_script, up to 20s within the 30s SHORT_TIMEOUT) for both services to reach Stopped before the reset. Also manually recovered the guest (sc.exe stop RustyNet, waited for Stopped, reset outbound to allow, removed RustyNet rules) so it starts clean. Verified: sc.exe stop stops the daemon in about 3s and the outbound reset stays Allow once the service is down; fmt/clippy/clean-probe tests pass.
